contexts.text: They precipitate themselves into more frightful punishments.
The states of lusts, or of evil, without any tempering by means of states of the affection of good, would be more atrocious than those of any animal.
He would otherwise have precipitated himself into a more frightful Hell...

Man is bent from evil to good in so far as he suffers himself to be bent in freedom, and that constantly, from the most frightful Hell, into which he labours with all his might to precipitate himself, into a milder one, if he cannot be led to Heaven.
Wherefore these are sent into a Hell the most frightful of all.
